result.headline: No clear control fault found; startup sensor and battery warnings plus estimator-like jumps are unexplained.
result.explanation: Actuator commands follow the pitch setpoint, and roll follows its setpoint with a 1.221 s lag, so there is no clear control or actuator fault. A sensor-health error at t=0.058 and abrupt steps in several estimated signals remain unexplained.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.058 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: The only error in the recording, logged once at start-up. It names no sensor and never repeats.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.058 s controller.event[mavros: Battery] mavros: Battery: WARN: Low voltage
evidence.shows: A low-voltage warning at the same instant. No voltage series is in the recording, so its size and effect cannot be checked.

evidence.quote: CHANGE vehicle.airspeed at t=1.834 s: 22.928 -> 14.277 m/s (step -8.651, 136.2x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: A one-sample airspeed step. Altitude steps 10.952 m at t=1.838 (line 55) and pitch steps 34.001 deg at t=2.784 (line 58). That looks like a sensor or estimator discontinuity, not only flight dynamics.

evidence.quote: TRACKING control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] vs vehicle.attitude[pitch]: typical |error| 8.584 deg, worst 38.317 at t=3.906 s; 3 window(s) above 25.753
evidence.shows: Pitch divergence is episodic. The roll setpoint-to-attitude best lag is 1.221 s at correlation 0.966, so roll is delayed, not unresponsive.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[7]] = 2036 for the whole recording (236 samples)
evidence.shows: Channels 0, 6 and 7 never move and yaw_rate is constant. These signals carry no information, and yaw behaviour cannot be assessed.

checked.check: Sequence of first departures from baseline around the first excursion (t 0-6 s)
checked.result: No signal left its baseline in order. The only events are the two start-up messages at t=0.058.

checked.check: Sequence around the later setpoint flips
checked.result: Throttle, ch2 and the roll setpoint move first at t=9.013 to 9.364. At t=45.17 altitude, yaw and both velocities step together before the actuators move. At t=59.251 the same signals step together.
Correlation 0.791, rising to 0.966 at a 1.221 s lag. Typical error is 6.366 deg. The worst error of 93.44 deg is at t=0.141, the first samples.
Correlation 0.778, 0.792 at lag -0.658 s. ch[2] is a plausible pitch-channel command.
Correlation -0.23, so ch[1] is not a simple roll output. The mixer mapping is not in the data.
Correlation 1.0, difference 0 us at every sample. They are identical commands, so they cannot show asymmetry between the two surfaces.
Throttle falls from 43 to 0 by t=74.479 and stays 0. Roll attitude stays between -3.169 and 7.088 deg. Airspeed stays between 14.152 and 18.604 m/s, so there is no visible loss of control.

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] diverged from its setpoint from t=0 to 0.201 s (peak |error| 93.44 deg)
effects.why: A first-sample transient, then roll catches up. It looks like initialisation or setpoint flip lag, not a cause.

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[pitch] diverged from its setpoint from t=2.936 to 4.715 s (peak |error| 38.317 deg)
effects.why: This follows the airspeed and altitude steps at t=1.834 and the pitch step at 2.784. It is a consequence of those, or of a manoeuvre.

effects.quote: CHANGE vehicle.velocity[x] at t=7.908 s: 14.66 -> 0.895 m/s (step -13.765, 91.8x its usual variation)
effects.why: Velocity and yaw steps coincide in time. They look like estimator or heading re-referencing, not a control cause.

next_action.action: Pull raw sensor status and battery voltage from the original flight log.
next_action.why: This separates a real sensor or power problem at start-up from a benign boot-time warning, and shows whether the state steps are estimator resets.
how: Open the original log (ulog/tlog) and read the SYS_STATUS sensor-health bitmask and battery voltage at the start of the flight.
Read estimator status or innovation flags around t=1.834, 2.784, 8.68, 45.17 and 59.251 s.
next_action.baseline: A normal flight of this airframe on the same battery.

outcomes.label: A named sensor unhealthy, or EKF resets at the steps
outcomes.means: The state steps are sensor or estimator faults, not true motion. Control tracking errors are then secondary.
outcomes.then: Identify the sensor and isolate it on the bench.

outcomes.label: All sensors healthy, voltage nominal, no resets
outcomes.means: The warnings are boot-time transients. The steps and lag are manoeuvre dynamics, and tuning and power areas stay open.
outcomes.then: Check controller gains and actuator mapping against the roll lag.

unknowns: The recording has no battery voltage, so the 'Low voltage' warning's size and effect cannot be assessed.
It is unknown which sensor the 'Sensor helth' error refers to, and whether the pitch and airspeed steps are real motion or estimator jumps.
Yaw rate is constant and the yaw setpoint is in another frame, so yaw control cannot be assessed.

data_requests.what: Battery voltage and current, and sensor-health status, for the whole flight
data_requests.why_needed: Decides whether the start-up warnings are real hardware problems or boot transients, and whether the state steps are estimator resets.

unobservable.fact: Whether the control surfaces physically moved as commanded
unobservable.why_it_matters: The actuator outputs are commands in microseconds. A stuck or weak servo would not show in this data.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Bench servo sweep, or surface position feedback if fitted.

unobservable.why_it_matters: It decides whether the sensor/estimator area is a real fault.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Read the SYS_STATUS bitmask in the raw log.

hypotheses.claim: A sensor-health problem or estimator resets cause the abrupt steps in airspeed, altitude, attitude, velocity and yaw.
hypotheses.because: A sensor-health error at t=0.058, plus coincident steps in several estimated signals at t=1.834, 45.17 and 59.251. Not tested against raw sensors.

hypotheses.claim: A servo or surface fault causes the tracking divergences.
hypotheses.because: Outputs follow the pitch setpoint (correlation 0.778) and show no stuck or saturated output. Commands were observed, not the surfaces.

hypotheses.claim: Roll lags its setpoint by 1.221 s, causing the divergence windows after setpoint flips.
hypotheses.because: Correlation rises from 0.791 to 0.966 at a 1.221 s lag. Divergences cluster after the large roll setpoint steps.

hypotheses.claim: A low battery voltage affects sensors or propulsion.
